title: Christopher Nolan Has Never Premiered a Film in India. That Changes This Month.
excerpt: The Odyssey brings Nolan, Matt Damon, and Tom Holland to Mumbai — with IMAX tickets hitting ₹3,300 and every screen locked for a month.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Christopher Nolan premieres his film 'The Odyssey' in India for the first time this July.
  • IMAX tickets for 'The Odyssey' are priced between ₹370 and ₹3,300, breaking records.
  • The film has secured a four-week exclusive IMAX window, blocking other releases.
  • A star-studded cast includes Matt Damon, Tom Holland, and Anne Hathaway.
  • The global release on July 17 aligns with the Mumbai premiere, emphasizing India's market importance.

The biggest filmmaker on the planet is about to do something he has never done before: bring his movie to Mumbai.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=P4H5H2QBWDU

Christopher Nolan, Matt Damon, and Tom Holland are confirmed to visit India this July for the premiere of The Odyssey — a reimagining of Homer's ancient epic shot entirely on brand-new IMAX cameras, with a reported budget north of $250 million and a cast list that reads like the Oscars front row. The event, scheduled at the PVR Icon IMAX at Phoenix Palladium, will mark the first time a Nolan-directed film has ever held an official premiere in India. Mumbai will sit alongside London, Paris, and New York on the global tour. Let that sink in for a moment.

> "It is no longer just about the box office collections; it is about establishing a direct connection with one of the most passionate movie-going audiences in the world." — Trade analysts on the India premiere

![Matt Damon — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/MattDamon-byPhilipRomano.jpg/3840px-MattDamon-byPhilipRomano.jpg)

Producer Emma Thomas is also expected to attend. For a filmmaker who has always let his work speak louder than any press tour, the decision to personally show up in Mumbai is a statement — not to the trade, but to the millions of Indian fans who have turned his films into communal events.

The Cast Is Absurd

> "For a single production to assemble this many A-listers is rare bordering on unprecedented."

Damon leads as Odysseus, the legendary king of Ithaca fighting his way home after the fall of Troy. Holland plays his son, Telemachus. And then the ensemble just gets ridiculous: Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong'o, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, and Jon Bernthal. For a single production to assemble this many A-listers is rare bordering on unprecedented. Universal Pictures is treating every premiere stop like a coronation, and the India leg feels especially earned.

Early reactions from preview screenings are calling the film a triumph, with career-best notices across the cast — even as the trailer's YouTube dislikes climbed past 566,000 on premiere day, a reminder that Nolan's ambition always divides before it conquers.

IMAX Tickets Are Selling Out — and Breaking Records

![Tom Holland — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f6/Tom_Holland_during_pro-am_Wentworth_golf_club_2023-2_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Advance bookings for IMAX screenings opened on June 8, and the numbers have been staggering. In Mumbai, prices range from ₹450 for morning slots at Inox Malad to ₹2,000 at Cinepolis Seawoods. In Pune, a single evening ticket is running at a jaw-dropping ₹3,000 to ₹3,300 — among the most expensive cinema tickets ever sold in the country. Delhi-NCR follows a similar pattern: standard seats at PVR Priya start at ₹450, while recliners climb to ₹1,400. Even the most affordable entry point, at Inox Paras, runs ₹370 for early morning shows.

The kicker? People are paying without blinking. Late-night IMAX shows are selling out within minutes.

Here's the detail that tells you just how seriously the industry is taking this film. The Odyssey has secured an exclusive IMAX window of at least four weeks — meaning every IMAX screen in India will play nothing but Nolan's film for a full month after release. The casualty? Spider-Man: Brand New Day, arriving just thirteen days later on July 31, will have no IMAX screens in India at all. For the first time in recent memory, a solo Spider-Man film will skip the format entirely.

![Anne Hathaway — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/da/Anne_Hathaway-_Press_conference_for_the_film_%22The_Devil_Wears_Prada_2%22_-_55194764955_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Sony Pictures India is steering Marvel fans toward 4DX, ScreenX, Dolby Cinema, and other premium large-format options instead. It's not a quality call — it's pure strategic real estate.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada, The Odyssey is the kind of event film that brings everyone to the cinema on opening night. The worldwide release on July 17 means you'll be watching it the same moment as the Mumbai premiere audience — a true global event.

Exclusive IMAX Lockout
›The Odyssey has a four-week exclusive IMAX window.
›Every IMAX screen in India will show only this film.
›Spider-Man: Brand New Day will not have IMAX screens available.
›Sony Pictures India redirects fans to other formats.

But there's something deeper here. Hollywood treating India as a marquee market, not an afterthought, changes the calculus for every major release that follows. When Nolan walks a Mumbai red carpet, it validates what Indian audiences have always known: this is one of the most passionate, discerning, and loyal movie-going cultures on Earth. The world is finally catching on.

The Odyssey opens in cinemas worldwide on July 17, 2026.
